title: Improve Your Pronunciation By 'Shadowing' Others
titleZh: 通过“影子跟读法”提升你的发音
credits: John Russell wrote this lesson for VOA Learning English. George Grow and Kelly Jean Kelly were the editors.

sentences.en: Many English learners can improve their pronunciation by listening carefully to native English speakers and trying to match the up-and-down movement of their sentences.
sentences.zh: 许多英语学习者可以通过仔细聆听英语母语者的发音，并努力匹配他们句子中起伏的语调来改善自己的发音。

sentences.en: That is the opinion of Marla Yoshida, an English as a Foreign Language teacher at the University of California, Irvine.
sentences.zh: 这是玛拉·吉田的观点，她是加州大学欧文分校的一名英语作为外语的教师。

sentences.en: Yoshida wants English learners to look for details that are important to native speakers.
sentences.zh: 吉田希望英语学习者去关注对母语者而言重要的细节。

sentences.en: These details are not only sounds, she notes.
sentences.zh: 她指出，这些细节不仅仅是发音。

sentences.en: Native speakers also communicate by using pauses, and by saying some words more forcefully than others.
sentences.zh: 母语者还会通过停顿，以及比其它词更用力地说出某些词来进行交流。

sentences.en: As a result, native speakers might not understand an English learner even if the learner pronounces sounds correctly.
sentences.zh: 因此，即使英语学习者发音准确，母语者也可能听不懂。

sentences.en: Yoshida says that English learners often study pronunciation by listening and repeating something from a recording.
sentences.zh: 吉田说，英语学习者常常通过听录音并跟读来学习发音。

sentences.en: Yoshida says that English learners need to do more than listen and repeat in order to improve their pronunciation:
sentences.zh: 吉田说，英语学习者需要做比听和跟读更多的事情，才能改善自己的发音：

sentences.en: “I've gradually gotten really interested in pronunciation because it's something that students have trouble with, but they don't always get a lot of really good instruction in it.
sentences.zh: “我逐渐对发音产生了浓厚的兴趣，因为这是学生们感到困难的地方，但他们通常得不到太多真正好的指导。

sentences.en: They just have someone say 'Listen to this recording and repeat … and now, aren't you better?' No!
sentences.zh: 他们只是有人告诉他们‘听这段录音并跟读……现在，你是不是更好了？’不对！

sentences.en: You're not necessarily better.
sentences.zh: 你未必会更好。

sentences.en: It takes more than that.”
sentences.zh: 这需要更多的东西。”

sentences.en: The problem with listen and repeat, says Yoshida, is that when people repeat, they are often not trying to sound like the other person.
sentences.zh: 吉田说，听和跟读的问题在于，当人们跟读时，他们往往并不试图让自己听起来像那个人。

sentences.en: “You think that when students are repeating after the teacher, or whatever, they're trying to sound exactly like that person, but they're not.
sentences.zh: “你以为当学生跟读老师，或做其他类似的事情时，他们是在试图完全模仿那个人的声音，但其实并非如此。

sentences.en: The sounds that you hear go into your brain … and your brain interprets them or filters them through the sound system of your own language, and what your brain ends up understanding is not everything – it's not what the speaker intended…
sentences.zh: 你所听到的声音进入你的大脑……你的大脑会对它们进行解读，或通过你自己语言的声音体系对它们进行过滤，而你的大脑最终理解的内容并非全部——它并不是说话者想要表达的意思……

sentences.en: You have to try to get past that filter and hear all of the details that are important to someone else.
sentences.zh: 你必须努力越过这层过滤，听清所有对他人而言重要的细节。

sentences.en: So you have to try to duplicate what the person is saying."
sentences.zh: 所以你必须努力复现那个人所说的所有内容。”

sentences.en: What details should you try to copy when you listen to an English speaker?
sentences.zh: 当你聆听英语说话者时，你应该努力模仿哪些细节？

sentences.en: Among others, the important details include pauses or breaths, which words to emphasize -- or give special attention to, and intonation – the up and down movement of your voice as you speak.
sentences.zh: 除了其它方面，重要的细节包括停顿或呼吸、要强调的词——即给予特别关注的词，以及语调——即你说话时声音的起伏变化。

sentences.en: English speakers, in particular, use a broad range of up and down movements in their voices.
sentences.zh: 英语说话者，尤其是这样，他们的声音会使用非常广泛的起伏变化。

sentences.en: These movements can be difficult for English learners to recognize and understand.
sentences.zh: 这些语速变化对英语学习者来说可能难以识别和理解。

sentences.en: Native English speakers might have difficulty understanding English learners when learners use a narrow range of their voice.
sentences.zh: 当英语学习者使用较窄的音域时，英语母语者可能会难以理解他们说的话。

sentences.en: In other words, native speakers have fewer vocal restrictions when they are speaking.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，母语者在说话时声音限制较少。

sentences.en: English learners also may use intonation patterns that are different from those in Standard English.
sentences.zh: 英语学习者还可能使用与标准英语不同的语调模式。

sentences.en: Studying how native speakers use intonation will help English learners better understand what native speakers do with their voices.
sentences.zh: 研究母语者如何使用语调，能帮助英语学习者更好地理解母语者如何运用他们的声音。

sentences.en: If English learners want to start improving their pronunciation, Yoshida suggests that they do an activity called shadowing.
sentences.zh: 如果英语学习者想开始改进发音，吉田建议他们进行一种名为"影子跟读"的活动。

sentences.en: “Shadowing means finding a short audio or video clip that you like… that's maybe 30 seconds long, one minute long, at most two minutes long, and listen to it.
sentences.zh: "影子跟读是指找一段你喜欢且较短的音频或视频片段……大约30秒长，1分钟长，最多2分钟长，然后反复听。

sentences.en: Listen to it a couple of times to get the meaning, and to hear where the speaker pauses, and what they emphasize … and what the intonation sounds like – because those are really important things too – not just the sounds.
sentences.zh: 听一两遍以理解内容，并听出发言人在哪里停顿、强调什么……以及语调听起来如何——因为这些同样非常重要——不仅仅是发音。

sentences.en: Pronunciation is much more than saying each sound correctly because you can say each sound correctly and still sound really hard to understand…
sentences.zh: 发音远不止把每个音发准，因为你可以把每个音都发准，却仍然听起来很难理解……

sentences.en: So, find a short clip, listen to it, mark things that you notice, then listen a few more times just to sort of let those sounds become a part of your brain, and then start imitating.
sentences.zh: 所以，找一段简短的片段，听它，标记你注意到的地方，然后再听几遍，让这些声音逐渐融入你的大脑，然后开始模仿。

sentences.en: And imitate trying to sound exactly like that person.”
sentences.zh: 并努力模仿，力求与那个人听起来一模一样。"

sentences.en: Here is a short example of what a shadowing activity could look like.
sentences.zh: 下面是一个影子跟读活动的简短示例。

sentences.en: The example comes from Martha Kolln's book Rhetorical Grammar*:
sentences.zh: 这个例子来自玛莎·科恩的《修辞语法》一书：

sentences.en: "One of the most important aspects of your expertise with sentences is your sense of rhythm."
sentences.zh: "你对句子掌握得最好的方面之一，就是你对节奏的感知。"

sentences.en: Listen to the sentence several times.
sentences.zh: 把这句话听几遍。

sentences.en: Then try to mark the intonation of the voice.
sentences.zh: 然后尝试标记声音的语调。

sentences.en: Listen for emphasized words.
sentences.zh: 注意听被强调的单词。

sentences.en: In the sentence, you can hear that some syllables are emphasized, while others are not.
sentences.zh: 在这句话中，你可以听到有些音节被强调，而有些则没有。

sentences.en: Overall, the voice falls after important syllables, notably at the end of the sentence.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，声音在重要音节后会下降，尤其在句末最为明显。

sentences.en: English sentences often emphasize words at the end of a sentence – the place where you usually find new information.
sentences.zh: 英语句子通常在句末强调单词——也就是你通常能找到新信息的地方。

sentences.en: The next time you are reading and listening to a story, try to mark the patterns of intonation that you hear.
sentences.zh: 下次你阅读并听故事时，试着标出你所听到的语调模式。

sentences.en: Remember, all our stories have audio, so you can print the story and do a shadowing exercise while listening to the story.
sentences.zh: 请记住，我们所有的故事都配有音频，所以你可以打印故事，并在听故事的同时进行跟读练习。

sentences.en: Give shadowing a try, and let us know how it works for you!
sentences.zh: 试试跟读吧，并告诉我们它对你是否有效！

sentences.en: I'm John Russell.
sentences.zh: 我是约翰·拉塞尔。

glossary.def: the way in which a word or name is pronounced
to make the sound of a word or letter with your voice
passes something through a filter to remove something unwanted
to make an exact copy of something
to give special attention to something : to place emphasis on something
the rise and fall in the sound of your voice when you speak
all the notes that a particular person can sing or that a particular musical instrument can make
any one of the parts into which a word is naturally divided when it is pronounced
